{"id":"bkt-sn7","title":"cognitive forcing on Check, calibration record, arm switch shipped","description":"PR #63 (feat/ros-cognitive-forcing) against main, not yet merged. PLAN-REVISION-2.md section 2a's design response to Bucinca, Malaya and Gajos (2021), Bansal et al. (2021), and Vaccaro, Almaatouq and Malone (2024): before the tutor's grounded feedback is shown on the Check tool, the learner now writes an explanation, rates their confidence on forcing.ts's 4-point LearnerConfidence scale, and predicts which of their own quoted sources their explanation rests on; the verdict holds server-side (forcing.ts's in-memory held-attempt store, ATTEMPT_TTL_MS 30 minutes, matching rate-limit.ts's best-effort posture) until both arrive on the same attemptId. workspace/route.ts's check action becomes two-phase (no attemptId submits and grades, holding the verdict; attemptId present calls revealPendingAttempt, the single gate that returns ok:false with no grade field until both a valid learnerConfidence and a non-empty sourcePrediction are present in the same request); consumePendingAttempt makes reveal single-use. computePredictionCorrect checks a source prediction against the node's own citation label in code, never asking the model. Calibration record: learnerConfidence, sourcePrediction, predictionCorrect land in the evidence jsonb per an updated EVIDENCE-SCHEMA.md; calibration.ts's computeCalibrationSummary (mean confidence against mean source-prediction correctness, forcing-gated check events only) is wired into GET /api/research-os/class and rendered on /research-os/class, confirmed untouched by other in-flight work via git log -3 --since='2 hours ago' -- src/app/research-os/class before adding it directly rather than leaving it as an unexposed server function. Arm switch: RESEARCH_OS_FORCING_ENABLED env var (default on) plus a nullable per-class graph.classes.forcing_enabled override (migration 20260910060000_research_os_forcing.sql) let a three-arm pilot turn forcing off on its comparison arm without a second deployment; every check evidence event carries forcingEnabled regardless of arm so analysis can group pilot data by arm from the evidence log alone; db.ts's loadForcingEnabledForLearner fails open (null) on any lookup error. Workspace page (page.tsx) Check card gains a third render phase: two grade-4-reading-level questions as native fieldset/legend/labeled radio-input groups (same accessible pattern /research-os/profile already uses), sourced from the learner's own \"sources I have quoted\" list; the reveal shows the learner's prediction beside the tutor's real citation and whether it matched. learning/research-os/study/INSTRUMENTS.md section 2 (the metacognitive confidence item) rewritten from its original after-the-verdict design to the shipped before-the-verdict placement; original text preserved verbatim in _intake/research-os-k12/DELETIONS.md. 28 new tests across scripts/test-research-os-forcing.ts (19, including the headline \"feedback cannot be fetched early\" case run directly against revealPendingAttempt, the production function the route calls) and scripts/test-research-os-calibration.ts (9), plus new onCheckResult/onProbeCheckResult coverage in scripts/test-research-os-evidence.ts; wired into npm run test:research-os. Merged origin/main after PRs landed concurrently (edge-inference LLM proposal review UI, prereq-ancestor rebuild); one conflict, package.json's test:research-os script chain, resolved keeping both sides' test invocations, plus one pre-existing meta-commentary/filler-adverb voice violation in a merged-in hypothesis-engine swarm findings file fixed so the pre-commit hook would pass. Gates green post-merge: npm ci, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build (both /research-os/class and /research-os/workspace confirmed in the manifest), npm run test:research-os (330/330 across 25 files), eslint on every file this pass touched, agf-lint-voice-src check and agf-lint-voice check clean on every touched file (fixed two banned words, one filler adverb, and six antithesis phrasings on the first pass). learning/research-os/WORKSPACE.md section 6 (new) and learning/research-os/CHANGE-LEDGER.md Iteration 22 carry the full account.\n\nsource: unknown","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:17Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:17Z"}

{"id":"bkt-q3x","title":"ros-14: faded guidance for low-prior-knowledge learners, worked examples, guidance switch shipped","description":"feat/ros-faded-guidance against main, not yet merged. A per-class research_os_guidance_enabled switch (migration 20260910080000_research_os_guidance.sql, plain not-null boolean, default true, OR-across-class-memberships) gates the whole feature per class, forcing the level to low when off. 27 new tests in scripts/test-research-os-guidance.ts covering computeGuidanceLevel, classifyCheckOutcome, nextGuidanceLevel, decideGuidanceEnabled, and firstHalfOfWorkedExample; wired into npm run test:research-os. Merged origin/main partway through (PR #63, cognitive forcing, merged concurrently and touched the same workspace/route.ts check case and workspace page): four conflicts resolved by combining both sides, a new shared computeGuidanceForNode helper serves both Check phases so guidance and forcing compose rather than one overwriting the other; migration renamed from 20260910060000 to 20260910080000 after colliding with PR #63's own 20260910060000_research_os_forcing.sql; GUIDANCE.md section 4 rewritten with the confirmed facts about PR #63's real forcing_enabled switch once visible (a plain research_os_guidance_enabled column was added on its own, since a class can run either pilot arm, both, or neither). learning/research-os/GUIDANCE.md (new) and a WORKSPACE.md section 7 addition carry the full design account. Gates green: npm ci, npx tsc --noEmit, npm run build, npm run test:research-os (full chain, 0 failures), eslint and agf-lint-voice-src check / agf-lint-voice check clean on every touched file.\n\nsource: unknown","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:17Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:17Z"}

{"id":"bkt-frqy","title":"ros-prime epic: prime decomposition of concepts, a dependency graph of irreducible primes, and a truth level from the factors","description":"Founder idea 2026-09-18, carries ros-25. Slices: 1 decomposition, signature, penetration, tier, and the PRIMES.md memo over the local graph; 2 the decompose-further queue with model-proposed factors held for review; 3 the truth level and network statistics; 4 the node page made-of section and map layers.\n\nsource: research-os-loop","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"epic","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:29Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:29Z"}

{"id":"bkt-0hzn","title":"ros: move the paging allowlist off path:line keys onto anchors","description":"scripts/research-os/paging-allowlist.ts keys each exception by `path:line` as paging-scan reports it. Every edit above a listed read shifts the key, and the gate then reports the read as unlisted and the entry as stale. {"id":"bkt-6gp6","title":"ros: teach the total-order paging rule about partial unique indexes","description":"scripts/research-os/graph-keys.ts declares every non-partial unique key in the graph schema and orderIsTotal checks an order against it. Partial indexes are left out, because a key that holds only under a predicate makes an order total only when the read pins that predicate to the value the predicate names. graph.evidence_source_admissions carries a unique (source_id, scope) where status = 'active', and quotableRevisions in src/lib/research-os/evidence-search/server.ts pins both scope and status='active', so that read is total under the partial key and the gate cannot see it. The read now carries the full key and costs one sort column, so nothing is broken. Fix when a second read needs it: record each partial key with its predicate column and required value, and count it only when the read pins that column to that value with eq().\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z"}

{"id":"bkt-gawe","title":"ros: check-code-citations resolves path:N and never a bare path","description":"scripts/check-code-citations.mjs matches CITE = /path:(\\d+)/, so a document naming a file with no line number is never resolved and the run reports 'every citation resolves'. Two documents named src/lib/research-os/import-storage.ts and supabase/migrations/20260922020000_research_os_import_files.sql, neither of which exists at that revision, under a sentence saying storage was built; the checker passed both. Adding a bare-path pass is four lines and finds 711 citations across the repo that resolve to nothing: 268 in learning/research-os/CHANGE-LEDGER.md, 62 in SOFTWARE-ATLAS.md, 36 in docs/PROBLEM-REGISTER.md, and a long tail. Not all are defects. A change ledger records what a path was, so naming a file that has since moved is its job, and the sample includes alias forms like @/data/world-indicators.js that the suffix resolver cannot follow. The work is the triage rather than the check: decide which trees the rule covers, teach the resolver the @/ alias, give a ledger an exemption marker, then turn it on. Shipping the check without that means writing 711 exemptions in a hurry, which is how six false reasons entered the paging allowlist.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z"}

{"id":"bkt-q7qw","title":"ros: graph.nodes visible_select never admits a grantee","description":"supabase/migrations/20260915000000_research_os_access.sql:102 writes `select 1 from graph.node_grants g where g.node_id = id and g.grantee_id = auth.uid()`. In that scope `id` binds to node_grants.id, so the live policy body reads `g.node_id = g.id`: it compares a grant's own primary key to the node the grant is for. Confirmed against the local catalog with `select qual from pg_policies where tablename='nodes' and policyname='visible_select'`. The clause can never match, so a grantee has never been admitted by row-level security on graph.nodes, and only public nodes and the owner's own are visible under it. Latent rather than live: `authenticated` holds no USAGE on schema graph, so no client reaches the policy and every read goes through a service-role route that applies read-access.ts instead. It becomes live the day schema usage is granted. Fix: a new migration that recreates the policy with `g.node_id = nodes.id`, plus a fixture that inserts a grant and asserts the grantee reads the node under `set local role authenticated`. Do not edit the 20260915 file, which is already applied.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z"}

{"id":"bkt-2lq0","title":"ros-import: reconcile an import_files row with bytes that are gone","description":"graph.import_files records an object in the research-os-imports bucket, and the two live on opposite sides of a boundary no foreign key crosses. An owner may delete the object under research_os_imports_own_delete while the row survives naming a path that resolves to nothing, and a consumer cannot tell that from a path that never existed. Deleting the account cascades the row away and leaves the bytes, because storage.objects references only storage.buckets, so an object stays with an owner uuid pointing at a user who no longer exists. Fix: a delete route that removes the object and marks the row in one call, a tombstone column so a run that recorded the input can say what happened, and account deletion that clears the objects before the cascade.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z"}

{"id":"bkt-a7vc","title":"ros-import: reap objects no import_files row records","description":"graph.import_upload_allowed caps an owner at 50 objects in the research-os-imports bucket that carry no graph.import_files row, which is what stops an open signup from being an unmetered 50 MiB object store. The cap bounds the damage and reclaims nothing. The uploader writes the bytes and then records them (src/app/research-os/(app)/import/page.tsx), so an attach that fails after a successful upload leaves an orphan, and an owner who accumulates 50 cannot upload until they delete their own objects. {"id":"bkt-tnlf","title":"ros: the outage gate marks 8 of 31 routes and a gateway 503 reaches all 31","description":"scripts/test-research-os-outage.ts marks a client call only when the route emits a transient code from its own handler or imports evidence-errors. Counted on the revision this bead was written against: 31 route directories, every one with a route.ts, of which the rule marks 8 (evidence-search, node, override, probe, production, review, state, workspace) and leaves 23 unmarked. Marking every route flags 36 calls across 17 files. Re-count before working it; the numbers moved three times in one day as the code moved, and an earlier version of this bead said 28 routes and 37 calls across 12 files, where the 28 was never right and the 12 was the number of lines printed by a truncated terminal command read back as a file count. isTransientOutage(503, null) returns true because a bare 503 comes from a gateway or a CDN, and a gateway sits in front of every route, so a client calling any of the 31 can be handed one and has to consult the rule. It is fixed. The rest have not been checked one by one, and the earlier claim that none was live was made from a sample. {"id":"bkt-beil","title":"ros: merge dev into a branch before a critic round","description":"Five review rounds on 2026-09-22 scored branches that were three to seven commits behind dev, so findings were raised against code dev had already superseded and repairs were written by hand for fixes dev already carried. fix/ros-dropped-errors was seven behind: its round-5 Critical, five new 503 codes whose readers render 'Research OS is unavailable on this deployment', is solved on dev by src/lib/research-os/outage.ts from PR #212, and the Quote error branch written during that round already existed on dev in a better form that reads provenanceRecorded and tells the learner to quote again before citing. dev's own gate refused the merge because the five codes were unclassified, which is the gate working. Rule: merge dev, resolve, run the chain, then request a round. A round is a measurement and a stale merge base measures the wrong artifact. Cost of not doing it here: hours of reimplementation across two sessions, and six of ten remaining client fixes on that branch already exist on two other branches.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z"}

{"id":"bkt-8xve","title":"ros: the three structural gates land as their own change, scored on their own","description":"The read gate (test-research-os-route-authorization), the paging gates (paging-scan, paging-discipline) and the outage gate (test-research-os-outage) were each edited inside product repairs across five branches, so every round a fix to the product carried an unscored gate revision with it. Three generations of each gate now exist across feat/ros-ai-access-read, fix/ros-outage-round4 and fix/ros-dropped-errors, and six client fixes are duplicated between them. The gates also became a defect source: PR #195 fell 8.40 to 7.83 to 6.88 over two rounds and every High in both drops was in the gate rather than in the code it guards. Round 12 found a SEALED check that can never fire, because the sealed set and the reader set are disjoint by construction, so it reported a proof nobody performed; and an exemption proof matched against comment-stripped source with strings kept, which reopened the round-11 exploit inside the same commit that closed it. The critic's summary is the design note to keep: a database test caught the loadConnections leak while the regex proof beside it caught nothing. Plan: freeze the gates where they stand, land the product repairs, then one change that reconciles the three generations into one, scored on its own, with behavioural tests rather than regex proofs wherever a decision can be exercised.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z"}

{"id":"bkt-i1tp","title":"ros-import: the per-owner storage limits are provisional and want a product decision","description":"graph.import_quota_gate refuses a write past 500 objects or 2 GiB for one owner in the research-os-imports bucket. Those two numbers were chosen so that a bound exists, and nobody has decided what a learner should be allowed to hold. They live in the migration as literals in the trigger body. 2 GiB at the 50 MiB per-object limit is about 40 full-size files or 500 small ones. The shape of the decision: what a learner holds, whether staff or a class hold more, whether the bound is per owner or per class, and what a person sees when they reach it. The mechanism is correct whatever the numbers are, since the gate locks the owner's row and counts every object and every byte, so changing them is editing two literals and re-running the migration. Until then an owner at the limit sees the Postgres check_violation message through the import page, which feat/ros-import-upload turns into a sentence about finishing or removing files.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z"}

{"id":"bkt-bpc1","title":"ros-frontend: Find keeps the previous step's sources when the learner moves along the path","description":"src/app/research-os/(app)/workspace/EvidenceFind.tsx has no effect on branch or targetNodeId, and the workspace renders it without a key, so the component stays mounted while `selected` changes. A learner searches on one step, clicks another step in the path, and the cards found for the first step stay on screen under the second. Quote would attach a source to a target it was never about, which is the provenance confusion the receipt contract exists to prevent. IMPLEMENTATION.md, UI behavior, asks for late responses to be ignored after a newer query or target change, and for no stale cards to look like the current answer. Fixed on fix/ros-find-target-change: an effect on [branch, targetNodeId] aborts the request in flight, moves the sequence so a late answer is dropped, and clears the cards. Covered by tests/e2e/evidence-search.spec.ts, which fails without the effect.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:38Z"}

{"id":"bkt-jm18","title":"ros-ai-find rollback gate: run the corpus rollback sequence end to end instead of asserting it","description":"learning/research-os/ai/OPERATING.md, Rolling back a corpus, states that between admitting the older revision and restarting the worker on its vectors, every request answers degraded and nothing serves the withdrawn revision. Each piece is covered on its own: the worker refuses a foreign corpus revision with stale_corpus (tools/evidence-search tests), the server answers a worker refusal from keyword ranking marked degraded (test-research-os-evidence-search.ts), and eligibility reads the admissions registry rather than the files. The three together, in that order, have never been run. To close it: build a second revision (a different --limit gives one), admit it, restart the worker on the first revision's vectors, and assert across the window that every response is degraded, that no card carries a source outside the admitted set, and that no response names the revision being rolled away from. Then restore the original admission. Blocked on nothing except a second built corpus. The Rollback gate in IMPLEMENTATION.md stays open until this runs.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z"}

{"id":"bkt-86tb","title":"ros-ai-find rollback window measured: nothing serves a retired source, and nothing degrades either","description":"Ran the sequence the earlier bead asked for. Built a 400-source revision beside the live 500-source one, admitted the smaller (413 rows active, 100 retired), left the server pinned to the larger corpus directory and the worker on its vectors, then searched. Result: every request answered hybrid and ok, and no retired source appeared in 14 cards across six queries. A query aimed at the retired material returned academy-biophysics-cryo-em-ctf, which stayed admitted, and excluded academy-biophysics-cryo-em-revolution and academy-biophysics-cryo-em-workflow, which were retired; after restoring the original admission the same query returned all three at ranks 1 to 3. The active set was restored byte-identical to a snapshot taken before the run. Two corrections to OPERATING.md: the safety property holds, by eligibility being resolved from the registry per request rather than by the worker refusing a stale revision; and the window does not degrade, because the worker compares the revision the server sends with its own and both are still the newer corpus. Search keeps full quality on whatever remains admitted. The remaining untested piece of the Rollback gate is step 2, the worker restarted onto older vectors while the server still loads the newer corpus.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z"}

{"id":"bkt-8e5c","title":"ros-ai-find rollback gate closed: both windows measured, and they behave differently","description":"Step 2 run on 2026-09-23, closing the piece the earlier bead named. Worker started on the 400-source revision's vectors while the server stayed pinned to the 500-source corpus directory. Every request answered mode lexical, status degraded, modelRevision null, five cards from checked keyword ranking; the worker's counters showed stale 3 and scored 0. No error reached a caller and the admissions table was never touched (513 active before and after). Together with the step 1 run this closes the corpus half of the Rollback gate in IMPLEMENTATION.md. The two windows are not alike, which the runbook now says: admitting the older revision narrows eligibility and keeps full quality, while restarting the worker onto older vectors drops the whole deployment to keyword ranking until step 3 points the server at the same revision. That asymmetry is the reason the runbook's order is the safe one. Still outside this: flag-off drain, which is covered by the route's own feature-off test, and restoring an allowed prior index, which is the same admit call measured in step 1.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-23","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z"}

{"id":"bkt-mvoy","title":"ros: every structural gate proves it fires on something","description":"Three checks shipped in one day could not fire on some input, and none of the three was found by a run of the check. SEALED asserted over two sets that are disjoint by construction, so the assertion could never fail. The paging rule matched column and table names with [a-z_]+, so a table whose name carries a digit never matched and its paged read left the rule without failing it. The parse-order rule tested each following statement's whole subtree text, so an ok check on any other response answered for the parse under test. The loud direction costs an hour. The silent direction costs nothing visible: the rule looks like coverage and is absent on the rows it cannot see, and no run reports that. Give each structural gate a case that fails when the gate narrows, in the gate's own file, next to the rule it guards. Three now carry one: paging-discipline pins the column-name class, error-scan pins the refusal arm against two empty shapes, and the render rule carries its defect plus three negative controls. The rest do not.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-23","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:39Z"}

{"id":"bkt-q7qw","title":"ros: graph.nodes visible_select never admits a grantee","description":"supabase/migrations/20260915000000_research_os_access.sql:102 writes `select 1 from graph.node_grants g where g.node_id = id and g.grantee_id = auth.uid()`. In that scope `id` binds to node_grants.id, so the live policy body reads `g.node_id = g.id`: it compares a grant's own primary key to the node the grant is for. Confirmed against the local catalog with `select qual from pg_policies where tablename='nodes' and policyname='visible_select'`. The clause can never match, so a grantee has never been admitted by row-level security on graph.nodes, and only public nodes and the owner's own are visible under it. Latent rather than live: `authenticated` holds no USAGE on schema graph, so no client reaches the policy and every read goes through a service-role route that applies read-access.ts instead. It becomes live the day schema usage is granted. Fix: a new migration that recreates the policy with `g.node_id = nodes.id`, plus a fixture that inserts a grant and asserts the grantee reads the node under `set local role authenticated`. Do not edit the 20260915 file, which is already applied.\n\nsource: bkt-nuc 2026-09-22","status":"deferred","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"gianyrox@gmail.com","created_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z","created_by":"gianyrox","updated_at":"2026-09-23T13:14:37Z"}

{"design":"Local prototype, v2 2026-09-29, answers critic round 1. Scope: a local command, no server, no hosted DB, no network. The advisor path is TF-IDF plus truncated SVD from prime_directions, fitted on the people file; no model is downloaded.
1 Inputs: --statement (Markdown or text in slice 1; PDF in slice 2) and --cv (slice 2). PDF limits: 20 MB, 40 pages, 30 s per file; pypdf first with decompression capped, then pdftotext called as pdftotext -l 40 -- <path> -; a PDF that yields under 200 characters fails with 'this PDF has no text layer, export it with text or pass Markdown'.
2 People source: default is the public advisor export from bkt-abwh (advisor_public, emails stripped). --people overrides with a local file. Output is always built in publishable mode: no email from any source reaches --out.
3 Directions: parsed from a Research Directions section (numbered or bulleted items), else the top 6 statement paragraphs; --directions overrides.
4 Writes: only to --out. On creation the command writes --out/.bucket-fit-marker holding a random id and the version. It refuses an --out that exists, is non-empty and has no marker, and refuses a symlinked --out. --forget deletes --out only when the marker is present and --out is not a symlink, a filesystem root, the home directory or the repo; it deletes files inside --out and never follows symlinks. The page embeds the ranked rows, both stars and the statement-derived direction labels; it does not embed the statement or CV text. No telemetry.
5 Validation (slice 3): --validate pairs.csv (advisor OpenAlex id, student statement path, split year). Leakage control: works co-authored by the advisor and the student are excluded by author id, and advisor text is time-split to works before the split year. Baselines: unwhitened TF-IDF cosine, random order, h-index order. Reports MRR and recall@1, 10 and 100 with n. The report states that it measures topical retrieval of the known advisor and not advising fit.
6 The bkt desktop app wraps the command as 'bkt fit' after bkt-p3l4 Phase 1, in its own PR.
Slices: 1 Markdown or text statement, --people, --out, marker-guarded --forget, blocked-socket test. 2 PDF and CV. 3 --validate with baselines.
Tests slice 1: marker written; refuse unmarked non-empty and symlinked --out; --forget refuses home, root, repo and unmarked; no email in output with emails in input; directions parsing with and without a section; socket blocked during the run."}

{"design":"Graph source: prerequisite edges in the academy graph (graph.learning_items and its edge table, 820 edges over 487 nodes from academy-import; canon prereqs via prereq_ancestor). The Lean result assumes an exact graph, so the planner uses reviewed/confirmed prerequisite edges only. Pending or low-confidence edges show as "suggested" and leave the order unchanged. Exactness is a data claim: the UI says "minimal for the reviewed graph" and reports unreviewed foundations as a typed warning.

Algorithm (src/lib/academy/prereq-path.ts, pure TS): target t, edges E, mastered set M. (1) C(t) = t plus all ancestors by reverse DFS. (2) M_C = M intersect C(t); check the target-local predicate (every mastered node in C(t) has its immediate prereqs in M). A violation returns a typed MasteryConflict. (3) Emit C(t) minus M_C in topological order (Kahn, ties by tier then id). Typed failures: Cycle, MissingNode, MasteryConflict, UnreviewedFoundation. Matches Learning.lean: RestrictedKnown, remaining_necessary, minimum_unit_distance. Unit cost only; weighted effort is out of scope.

Mastery: mastered = fused mastery threshold from src/lib/academy/mastery.ts (the one rollupBranch uses) over engine state from progress-store readLocal, merged with server progress when online. Offline, the graph comes from the bundled corpus (corpus.ts), so the bkt app plans with no network.

Tasks: content-pack multiple-choice items (k=4), graded by gradeChoice. Each probe is 40 unseen items in 20 pairs matched on pack difficulty tier and AI correctness. A seeded coin sends one item of each pair to solo (H), the other to paired (J). Scores are guess-corrected: s = (c - 1/k) / (1 - 1/k).

A, AI alone: scored once at pack build, online, through the Batches API. Model claude-opus-5-5 at effort low, one run; it accepts no temperature, so the recorded answer and one-line rationale are frozen in the pack with model id and date. Cost at about 250 input and 300 output tokens per item (thinking included): 2,000 items = 0.5M in x $4 + 0.6M out x $20 = $14, $7 at batch rates. A 200-item pilot measures real usage first (~$0.70). A for a probe = guess-corrected AI score on its J items only.

Pair: on each J item the person gets a 20 s solo window, then sees the frozen AI answer and rationale and may accept or override. accepted_ai is stored per answer.

Retest at t+7d: the first launch after due_at runs all 40 items unaided, choices reshuffled.
- Retention R = H items at t+7d minus H(t).
- Learning L = J items at t+7d minus H(t), valid because the halves are matched.
- Dependence flag: J > H while L <= 0.

Statistics: per probe m = J / max(H, A), null when the max is below 0.1. Per-person numbers are descriptive only: pooled m, R and L with bootstrap 95% CIs over items, labelled with n. At 20 items per condition a probe SE is about 0.11. Detecting J - H = 0.10 at two SE needs about 200 items per condition, so a per-person claim needs 10 probes plus retests (400 items). The screen shows no trend line before 5 probe-plus-retest pairs.

Bank: 5 pairs need 200 unseen items, 10 need 400. The pack must hold 400 AI-scored items before hai mode opens.

Consent and data: one consent screen on first run; nothing leaves the device; bkt hai --wipe and a manual --export json. Tables hai_probe(id, t, due_at, seed, pack_version) and hai_answer(probe_id, item_id, pair_id, condition solo|pair|retest, correct, accepted_ai, ms), encrypted like attempts.

User sees: H, J, A after each probe; history with m, R, L, their CIs and the n counter.

Tests: pair matching and balance, guess correction, m, R, L math with guards, retest gating under an injected clock, consent gate, wipe, bootstrap CI on fixed data.

First slice: the 200-item pilot batch, schema, one 40-item probe with matched halves, H/J/A shown, due_at stored. Goal: prove the pipeline and measured cost. Retest and stats next."}

{"design":"Home: packages/bkt (offline TUI, WAL SQLite, AES-GCM columns). New mode: bkt hai. Rev 3.

Frozen bank: buildQuestion draws distractors per seed and the 998-item pack stores no choices. A one-time step freezes 3 distractors per item (seeded buildQuestion, then stored) into hai_bank(item_id, stem, choices[4], answer, tier, pack_version). hai mode shows only frozen questions, shuffling display order alone. A is scored on that exact frozen question, making it an item property.

Probe: 40 unseen bank items in 20 pairs matched on tier and AI correctness; a seeded coin sends one of each pair to solo (H), one to paired (J). Guess-corrected score s = (c - 1/4) / (3/4).

A, AI alone: Batches API, claude-opus-5-5, effort low, one run (no temperature on this model). Answer and one-line rationale are frozen with model id and date. About $14 for 998 items, $7 batched; a 200-item pilot measures usage first (~$0.70). Probe A = mean s of the AI on its J items.

Pair: on J items a 20 s solo window, then the frozen AI answer and rationale; accept or override; accepted_ai stored.

Feedback policy: no correctness shown on any hai item until its retest ends, and hai items never enter FSRS review. Between t and t+7d the only exposure is the AI answer on J items, so retention (H items) and learning (J items) stay separate. Scores and answers appear after the retest.

Retest at t+7d, unaided, all 40:
- R = s(H items, t+7d) - s(H, t)
- L = s(J items, t+7d) - s(H, t), with matched halves
- Dependence flag when the 95% CI of J - H lies above 0 and the CI of L includes or lies below 0.

Metrics: primary D = J - max(H, A). Secondary is the founder ratio m = J / max(H, A), shown beside D and null when the max < 0.1. Bootstrap over matched pairs (resample pairs, keep both items) for every CI.

Precision: on the guess-corrected scale at p = 0.5, a 95% CI half-width of 0.10 on J - H needs about 340 items per condition (50% chance to exclude 0 at a true 0.10); 80% needs about 680. {"design":"Plan v1 2026-09-30. Rule: a screen ships in the window only when its data is local and it needs no Supabase, pgvector, torch or network. Research OS pages call /api/research-os/* backed by Supabase, so each ported screen gets a /local/* route over bkt.db or bundled JSON.

Window, offline:
- Learn, prerequisite path, grip sphere: done in 1b; reuse src/lib/academy prereq-path and grip-sphere, katex 280 KB.
- Quiz and review: done.
- Work quiz: port lib/research-os/work-quiz logic to /local/work-quiz; answers in a new bkt.db table.
- Canon explorer globe and circle: bundle bucket-canon (5.3 MB) as a pack; lazy chunk with three and react-three (~900 KB gz); textures 5.5 MB cut to one 2k map (~1.5 MB).
- Solvability atlas, software atlas, patents, status: static JSON (128/172/8 KB), reuse page components.
- Human-AI multiplier: packages/bkt/src/hai already local; add a window view over HaiStore.
- Advisor review and fit-me: people file picked through /local/pick, parsed in serve, never uploaded; reuse tools/profile-builder and pi-fit scoring ported to TS; results in bkt.db.
- Workspace and notes: notes, pins and state in bkt.db; drop search, evidence search and words.
- History and evolution: read-only local snapshot of the user's own productions from bkt.db; the global graph stays web.

CLI only:
- bkt analyze with helix: Python 3 and numpy on the host; the window shows the report list from `bkt analyses` and starts a run through a /local/analyze job route.
- Hypothesis engine: the window calls hte-serve at 127.0.0.1:8420 only when /health answers; otherwise the tab is hidden. Nothing bundled (17 MB tree plus Python).

Dropped from the window: prime directions (faiss, sentence-transformers, torch, GBs), attend (vector search), class and home (multi-user DB), import (Supabase storage), nsm, roadmap (staff), workbench (server).

Budget: AppImage now 35 MB. Adds: canon pack 5.3 MB, textures 1.5 MB, UI to ~3 MB, atlases 0.3 MB. Estimate 45 MB. Over 150 MB only with a bundled Python runtime and numpy (~90 MB) or torch; neither ships. UI stays under the 8 MB gate with the globe as a lazy chunk. Memory: serve under 150 MB RSS; globe under 300 MB in the window.

Navigation: sidebar groups Learn (Learn, Quiz, Review, Work quiz), Explore (Canon, Solvability, Software), Research (Workspace, History, Advisor, Multiplier), Tools (Analyze, Hypotheses when hte-serve is up), Import.

Security: same serve auth, header token, Host and Origin checks, CSP adds 'wasm-unsafe-eval' only if the globe needs it. File access through /local/pick opaque handles; hte-serve proxied through serve so the window keeps one origin.

Reuse: shared logic moves into src/lib with no next/* imports; page components are split into a pure view plus a data hook, and the hook takes a web or local adapter.

Slices:
2a static atlases, status, sidebar groups.
2b canon pack plus circle, then globe lazy chunk, size gate check.
2c multiplier view, analyze job route and report list.
2d work quiz and workspace notes in bkt.db, migration 4.
2e advisor and fit-me over a picked people file.
2f history snapshot, hte-serve proxy.
"}

{"design":"Plan v2 2026-09-30, supersedes v1. Rule: the window runs a screen offline when its data is local and it needs no Supabase, pgvector or network. Heavy compute runs as host-Python jobs,. Each ported screen reads /local/* over bkt.db, bundled JSON or a picked file handle.

Window, offline:
- Learn, prerequisite path, grip sphere, quiz, review: shipped.
- Work quiz: source is a picked .beads/issues.jsonl plus the local git log of a picked repo; tab hidden when neither is set.
- Canon globe and circle: bucket-canon pack (5.3 MB); three and react-three as a lazy chunk (~900 KB gz); one 2k texture (~1.5 MB).
- Solvability, software, patents, status: static JSON (0.3 MB).
- Human-AI multiplier: view over the existing HaiStore.
- Advisor review and prime directions: viewer for precomputed advisor-review and prime-direction JSON opened through a /local/pick handle.
- Workspace notes: notes, pins and state in bkt.db.
- History: local snapshot of the user's own productions.

Host-Python jobs, started from the window through a /local/jobs route:
- bkt analyze with helix (numpy).
- Fit-me and advisor review (TF-IDF plus randomized SVD: numpy, scipy, sklearn). pi-fit embeddings need sentence-transformers and stay optional; missing deps show an install hint. No TS port of pi-fit scoring.
- Hypothesis engine: tab shows only when hte-serve at 127.0.0.1:8420 answers /health; serve proxies it.

Dropped from the window: attend (vector search), class and home (multi-user), import (Supabase storage), nsm, roadmap, workbench.

People-file privacy: bkt.db keeps publishable rows only; emails, tracker notes and statement text stay in the picked file and are never copied. People tables are excluded from hub sync by a table allowlist. `bkt forget people` deletes them and writes a marker; a later import refuses rows the marker covers unless re-picked with confirmation.

Budget: AppImage 35 MB now, estimate 45 MB after the canon pack, texture and UI (~3 MB). Only a bundled Python runtime with numpy and scipy (~120 MB) or torch would pass 150 MB; neither ships. Memory: serve under 150 MB RSS, globe under 300 MB.

Navigation: sidebar groups Learn (Learn, Quiz, Review, Work quiz), Explore (Canon, Solvability, Software), Research (Advisor, Prime directions, Workspace, History, Multiplier), Jobs (Analyze, Fit-me, Hypotheses), Import.

Security: same serve auth, header token, Host and Origin checks, per-route body caps; files only through opaque /local/pick handles; jobs run a fixed allowlist of commands with argv arrays, never a shell string.



Slices:
2.0 Each reused screen splits into a pure view plus a data hook. A shared typed contract in src/lib/research-os/contract.ts, web and local adapters, contract tests run the same fixtures against /api/research-os and /local, plus web regression tests on the current pages.
2a Advisor review and prime-directions viewer, people privacy and forget.
2b Jobs route: analyze, fit-me, advisor review.
2c Static atlases, status, sidebar groups.
2d Canon circle, then globe lazy chunk, size gate check.
2e Work quiz from picked beads and git log, workspace notes, migration 4.
2f Multiplier view, history snapshot, hte-serve proxy.
"}

{"design":"## Legal Path
Packet in nonprofit-application/ is a draft (2026-04-14): no entity, EIN, sponsor, or filing. Bridge: a comprehensive (Model A) fiscal sponsor, first choice CS&S, SFC or NumFOCUS, fallback HCB at 7%; OCF closed. Donations to the sponsor are deductible from day one. Path B (Delaware nonstock, 1023-EZ) runs in parallel per 07-FORM-1023-EZ-WORKSHEET.md. LAWYER: sponsor agreement, UBI status of citation fees, 1023-EZ timing against the $50K receipts cap.
Pass-through model: donors give to named topic funds; Bucket keeps variance power and final grant discretion. A donor recommends, the board decides. Earmarked gifts routed to a specific person fail the deductibility test (Rev. Rul. 63-252, IRS Pub. 526 https://www.irs.gov/publications/p526). A DAF is a separate sponsor-org regime under IRC 4966 (https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/charitable-organizations/donor-advised-funds); skip it for v1. LAWYER: fund-agreement language.
State registration: charitable solicitation registration in NY, CA and other solicitation states before national asks; the sponsor usually covers this under Model A. LAWYER: confirm.

## Donor Flow
Funds map 1:1 to canon branches (01-mathematics to 07-mind) and to Research OS productions, including a magazine issue link ("fund this topic"). A General Fund is the default and lets Bucket allocate by the expected-discovery ranking. Stripe card first, receipts carry the IRC 170(f)(8) written acknowledgment: amount, "no goods or services provided", sponsor EIN (Pub. 1771 https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1771.pdf).

## Reaching Researchers
Grants to individuals need an objective, nondiscriminatory selection process with written criteria and follow-up reports (IRS guidance on grants to individuals, https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/private-foundations/grants-to-individuals; 4945(g) is the private-foundation bar and a good default). Institutional grantees get paid through their university or a fiscal agent. Every grant gets a signed agreement with a report-back and a use restriction. LAWYER: whether the sponsor or Bucket runs selection.

## Impact Reporting
Reuse reports/Bucket education market and impact.md for education outcomes and _intake/ideas/EXPECTED-DISCOVERY-OBJECTIVE-THEORY.md plus IMPACT-ESTIMATE-METHOD.md for research: per-fund probability, magnitude and persistence, skeptical prior floor. Quarterly public report per fund: dollars in, grants out, outputs, updated estimate.

## Cost-Effectiveness Framing
State expected discoveries per $10K per fund, with GiveWell-style explicit models, skeptical adjustment and optimizer's-curse correction (https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness/cost-effectiveness-models; https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness/uncertainty-optimizers-curse). Use 80,000 Hours scale, neglectedness and tractability to choose which funds exist (https://80000hours.org/articles/problem-framework/). Named uncertainty: no track record, discovery counts are subjective, and counterfactual funding is unknown. Publish ranges and the floor.

## x402 and Payments
Citation fees stay program-service revenue routed to authors; donations stay a separate ledger with no return benefit. x402 USDC gifts are noncash property gifts needing fair-market valuation and possibly Form 8283 above $500; accept them only after the sponsor agrees. LAWYER: crypto gift acceptance and UBI.

## First Slice
1. Send the packet to CS&S and HCB this month.
2. On acceptance, one General Fund plus one topic fund (05-biophysics) on a single donate page, Stripe through the sponsor, sponsor-issued receipts.
3. One $2-5K pilot grant by written criteria with a public report."}

State registration: the sponsor registers for charitable solicitation.

Topic funds, one per canon branch (01-mathematics to 07-mind), each with open selection, plus a General Fund. A magazine issue links to its branch fund. Donor copy describes the use of funds and the selection process, with no impact claims. The sponsor issues receipts under IRC 170(f)(8) (Pub. 1771, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p1771.pdf).

- Founder recuses from any grant to himself, family, AGFarms or related parties (05-CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST-POLICY.md).
- An independent panel of at least 3 people with no ties to Bucket scores applications; the sponsor approves.
- Written criteria are published before any solicitation (https://www.irs.gov/charities-non-profits/private-foundations/grants-to-individuals).
- The founder assigns domain, code and wallet to the sponsor, later the entity.

Open call per fund, published rubric, signed grant agreement with a use restriction and a report-back. University researchers are paid through their institution.

Internal allocation uses the expected-discovery objective (_intake/ideas/EXPECTED-DISCOVERY-OBJECTIVE-THEORY.md) and the education model (reports/Bucket education market and impact.md). Quarterly public report per fund: dollars in, grants out, outputs.

Internal, GiveWell-style explicit models with skeptical adjustment (https://www.givewell.org/how-we-work/our-criteria/cost-effectiveness/cost-effectiveness-models). 80,000 Hours scale, neglectedness and tractability decide which funds open (https://80000hours.org/articles/problem-framework/). Named uncertainty: no track record, subjective discovery counts, unknown counterfactual. Publish ranges after a year of data.

## First Slice
1. Weeks 0-2: apply to PPF and CS&S; HCB as fallback. Budget 5-10% fee, PPF $5K deposit.
2. Weeks 2-4: publish CRITERIA.md (eligibility, rubric, panel names, recusal rule); recruit the panel.
3. Weeks 4-12: on signing, assign assets, open General Fund plus 05-biophysics fund.
4. Pilot: $5K, two $2.5K grants by open call, panel-scored, sponsor-approved, public report."}

{"design":"# Marketing corpus plan

Base: origin/dev 09cfa401f. Branch feat/ros-marketing-corpus, PR into dev. Covers bkt-ixi6.

## Outcome

A signed-in Research OS user drops an ad-platform export or any table file on /research-os/import/marketing, gets a marketing report (funnel metrics, CAC, LTV, cohorts, channel mix, attribution, trend, seasonality, anomalies), and can delete the file and every derived row. The same file passed to `bkt analyze` in the desktop app produces the same marketing section from the same Python code.

## One analysis core

New package `packages/bkt/analyze/marketing/` (stdlib plus numpy, the deps bkt_analyze.py already has):

- `readers.py`: XLSX and PDF table readers that return (header, rows) for `bkt_analyze.read_table`, which gains `.xlsx` and `.pdf` branches. CSV, TSV, JSON, JSONL and Parquet stay as they are.
- `adapters.py`: header fingerprints and column maps per platform.
- `schema.py`: the canonical record and the normalizer.
- `metrics.py`: every metric below.
- `report.py`: JSON section `marketing` plus Markdown `## Marketing`.

`bkt_analyze.py` calls `marketing.run(header, rows)` after the form check whenever an adapter or the generic entity detector matches, and adds `--marketing auto|on|off` (default auto). Report schema stays `bucket.analysis/1` with an additive `marketing` key, so the desktop analyze view and the jobs view keep rendering.

Web runs the same file: route `POST /api/research-os/marketing` spawns `python3 packages/bkt/analyze/bkt_analyze.py <tmpfile> --no-helix --marketing on --out <tmpdir>` under the local-first setup. `BKT_ANALYZE_PYTHON` names the interpreter; unset (Vercel) returns 503 `analysis_local_only` with copy that points to the desktop app. One code path, two callers; a parity test runs every fixture through both the CLI and the route handler and compares the `marketing` JSON.

## Formats

- XLSX: stdlib `zipfile` plus `xml.etree` reader of the first worksheet (or `--sheet N`). Reads cached `<v>` values and shared strings only; `<f>` elements are ignored, so no formula runs and a formula cell with no cached value reads as missing and raises `W_FORMULA_UNCACHED`. Guards before parsing: magic `PK\x03\x04`, `[Content_Types].xml` present with the spreadsheetml main type, at most 2,000 zip members, total uncompressed at most 200 MB, per-member ratio at most 100, no DOCTYPE in any parsed part (rejects entity expansion), macro-enabled parts (`vbaProject.bin`) rejected with `E_XLSX_MACRO`. Dates from serials use the 1900 system, or 1904 when `workbookPr date1904` is set. Cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` keep their text and are tagged in the report; nothing re-exports them to a spreadsheet.
- PDF tables: bounded worker subprocess (`marketing/pdfworker.py`, same pattern as `prime_directions/pdfworker.py` from PR #390): pypdf `extract_text(extraction_mode="layout")`, 40 pages, 60 s wall, RLIMIT_AS 1 GiB, pypdf stream caps set as in PR #390. Lines split into cells on runs of 2+ spaces; the header is the first line whose cell count equals the modal count; rows with other counts are dropped and counted in `W_PDF_ROWS_DROPPED`. Scanned PDFs with no text layer fail with `E_PDF_NO_TEXT`. Accuracy is empirical and measured on the fixtures only; the report says so.

## Adapters

Each adapter has `required` header tokens (all must appear after normalization: lowercase, currency suffix stripped, punctuation collapsed), `optional` tokens, and a column map into the canonical schema. Score = matched required plus 0.25 per optional; highest score wins, ties go to the generic detector. Preamble handling: skip leading `#` lines (GA4) and search the first 15 rows for the header (Google Ads title rows).

| Platform | Required fingerprint | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Ads | campaign name, amount spent, impressions, reporting starts | ad facts |
| Google Ads | campaign, cost, impr., clicks | ad facts |
| GA4 | session default channel group or first user default channel group, sessions | traffic facts |
| Shopify orders | name, financial status, total, created at | transactions |
| Stripe payments | id, amount, created date (utc), status | transactions |
| HubSpot deals | record id, deal stage, amount, close date | transactions |

Fixtures: one synthetic export per platform under `packages/bkt/analyze/tests/fixtures/marketing/`, generated by `make_marketing_fixtures.py` from a fixed seed, with invented campaign names, `example.com` emails and `cus_test_` ids. No real customer data. Each fixture has an expected-output JSON checked by test. XLSX and PDF fixtures are generated from the same seed (XLSX written by the stdlib writer in the fixture script; PDF written by a minimal PDF text writer in the script, so no new dependency).

## Canonical schema

`marketing.v1` record: `date` (ISO day), `platform`, `channel`, `campaign`, `spend`, `currency`, `impressions`, `clicks`, `sessions`, `conversions`, `revenue`, `customer_id`, `order_id`, `status`. Two grains: `ad` rows (date x campaign facts) and `txn` rows (one per order or payment). Refunded, failed and canceled statuses are excluded from revenue and counted. Currency: a single currency per file is required for money metrics; mixed currencies raise `W_MIXED_CURRENCY` and money metrics are reported per currency with no conversion. Customer ids are hashed with a per-run random salt before they enter the report, so the report carries no raw email or id.

## Metrics

Definitions become Lean in a new module `lean/BucketMath/Marketing.lean` over `Rat`, added to the manifest by `bm.py check --write`. Division by zero returns null with a reason.

| Metric | Formula | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| CTR | clicks / impressions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr], bounded by [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr_le_one] when clicks <= impressions |
| CPC | spend / clicks | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpc] |
| CPA | spend / conversions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa_mul] (CPA x conversions = spend) |
| ROAS | revenue / spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas_ge_one_iff] |
| CAC | spend in period / new customers first seen in period | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cac] |
| LTV | mean revenue per customer over the observed window, historical only | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ltv_hist]; no predictive LTV, the report states the window |
| Cohorts | customers grouped by first-order month; retention = share with an order in month k | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.retention_le_one] |
| Channel mix | channel spend / total spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.mix_sum_one] |
| Attribution | last-touch and linear over the channel column present in the file; no path data means last-touch by row channel | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.last_touch_conserves], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.linear_conserves] |
| Trend | OLS slope on daily totals, reusing `trend_season` | [bm:BucketMath.Project.pythagoras_orthonormal] for the residual split |
| Seasonality | ACF peak on residuals, reusing `find_season`; weekday profile when >= 28 days | [empirical: 2/sqrt(n) white-noise bound, Box and Jenkins 1976, tests/test_marketing.py] |
| Anomalies | robust z on daily totals: abs(x - median) / (1.4826 x MAD) > 3.5 | [empirical: Iglewicz and Hoaglin 1993 cutoff, tests/test_marketing.py] |

No causal claims. Attribution is labelled a heuristic.

## Storage and privacy

- Upload reuses PR #390's path and the existing import page code: browser hashes, uploads to private bucket `research-os-imports` under `<owner>/<sha256>`, `POST /api/research-os/import` verifies bytes and records `graph.import_files`. RLS already restricts storage and rows to owner or grantee; the quota trigger caps 500 objects and 2 GiB per owner.
- Size: the bucket takes 50 MB; marketing analysis caps the file at 25 MB and 1,000,000 rows, checked server side before the spawn.

| Platform | Required fingerprint | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Ads | campaign name, amount spent, impressions, reporting starts; optional purchases, purchases conversion value | ad facts |
| Google Ads | campaign, cost, impr., clicks; optional conversions, conv. value | ad facts |
| GA4 | session default channel group or first user default channel group, sessions | traffic facts |

```
graph.marketing_reports (
  id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(),
  import_id uuid not null references graph.imports(id) on delete cascade,
  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  input_digest text not null,        -- sha256 over the sorted file sha256 list
  analyzer_version text not null,    -- pysrc version hash
  key_id text not null,
  iv bytea not null, ciphertext bytea not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (import_id, input_digest, analyzer_version)
)
```

Insert uses `on conflict do nothing` then reads the row, so a double click or retry returns the same report. `GET /api/research-os/marketing?import=<id>` decrypts and returns the saved report. Storage removal failure returns 502 and leaves rows so a retry can finish. Account deletion cascades through `auth.users`.

- Web: `src/app/research-os/(app)/import/marketing/page.tsx` (staff-only at launch) reuses the import page's hashing, upload and attach helpers (extracted to `src/lib/research-os/import-client.ts`, the import page switches to it with no behavior change), then calls the marketing route and renders the report with a delete button. - SQL test `supabase/tests/research_os_marketing_reports.sql`: RLS denies another owner, cascade on import delete.
- Lean: `bm.py check` passes with the new module.
- Existing suites: `packages/bkt/analyze/tests`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `tsc`.

Additive: one migration (`graph.marketing_reports`, service-role only, cascade), new route, new page, new Python modules. Staff-only at launch through the existing gate. Rollback: revert the PR and drop the table; no existing table changes.

## Deferred beads

Filed before the build with `needs-founder` and `source-agent`: desktop jobs allowlist and 16 MB cap after #429; desktop report encryption; Google Sheets link import; multi-touch paths from GA4 path exports; currency conversion; shared rate limiter for a multi-process host."}

| Platform | Required fingerprint | Grain |

| Meta Ads | campaign name, amount spent, impressions, reporting starts; optional purchases, purchases conversion value | ad facts |

Preamble handling: skip leading `#` lines (GA4) and search the first 15 rows for the header (Google Ads title rows).

| Platform | Required fingerprint | Grain |
|---|---|---|
| Meta Ads | campaign name, amount spent, impressions, reporting starts; optional purchases, purchases conversion value | ad facts |
| Google Ads | campaign, cost, impr., clicks; optional conversions, conv. value | ad facts |
| GA4 | session default channel group or first user default channel group, sessions | traffic facts |
| Shopify orders | name, financial status, total, created at | transactions |
| Stripe payments | id, amount, created date (utc), status | transactions |
| HubSpot deals | record id, deal stage, amount, close date | transactions |

Joins across files: one analysis takes up to 8 files from one import. Ad-grain files give spend, impressions, clicks and platform-reported conversions and value by day and channel. Transaction files give orders, customers and revenue by day, and a channel when the file has one (HubSpot original source, Shopify referring site or UTM source when present). Channel names map through a fixed table (facebook, instagram and meta to `paid_social_meta`; google, adwords and cpc to `paid_search_google`; others to their lowercased name). Blended CAC and blended ROAS use total spend over the shared date range against transaction revenue and new customers in that range; per-channel ROAS uses platform-reported value when present and joined transaction revenue by channel otherwise, each labelled with its source. Metrics that lack their inputs return null with a reason naming the missing file type.

Fixtures: one synthetic export per platform under `packages/bkt/analyze/tests/fixtures/marketing/`, generated by `make_marketing_fixtures.py` from a fixed seed, with invented campaign names, `example.com` emails and `cus_test_` ids. No real customer data. Each fixture has an expected-output JSON checked by test, and the pair Meta plus Shopify has non-null CAC, ROAS and LTV in its expected output. XLSX and PDF fixtures are generated from the same seed (XLSX written by the stdlib writer in the fixture script; PDF written by a minimal PDF text writer in the script, so no new dependency).

## Canonical schema

`marketing.v1` record: `date` (ISO day), `platform`, `channel`, `campaign`, `spend`, `currency`, `impressions`, `clicks`, `sessions`, `conversions`, `revenue`, `customer_id`, `order_id`, `status`. Two grains: `ad` rows (date x campaign facts) and `txn` rows (one per order or payment). Refunded, failed and canceled statuses are excluded from revenue and counted. Currency: a single currency per file is required for money metrics; mixed currencies raise `W_MIXED_CURRENCY` and money metrics are reported per currency with no conversion. Customer ids are hashed with a per-run random salt before they enter the report, so the report carries no raw email or id.

## Metrics

Definitions become Lean in a new module `lean/BucketMath/Marketing.lean` over `Rat`, added to the manifest by `bm.py check --write`. Division by zero returns null with a reason.

| Metric | Formula | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| CTR | clicks / impressions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr], bounded by [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ctr_le_one] when clicks <= impressions |
| CPC | spend / clicks | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpc] |
| CPA | spend / conversions | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cpa_mul] (CPA x conversions = spend) |
| ROAS | revenue / spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.roas_ge_one_iff] |
| CAC | spend in period / new customers first seen in period | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.cac] |
| LTV | mean revenue per customer over the observed window, historical only | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.ltv_hist]; no predictive LTV, the report states the window |
| Cohorts | customers grouped by first-order month; retention = share with an order in month k | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.retention_le_one] |
| Channel mix | channel spend / total spend | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.mix_sum_one] |
| Attribution | last-touch and linear over the channel column present in the file; no path data means last-touch by row channel | [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.last_touch_conserves], [bm:BucketMath.Marketing.linear_conserves] |
| Trend | OLS slope on daily totals, reusing `trend_season` | [bm:BucketMath.Project.pythagoras_orthonormal] for the residual split |
| Seasonality | ACF peak on residuals, reusing `find_season`; weekday profile when >= 28 days | [empirical: 2/sqrt(n) white-noise bound from Box and Jenkins 1976, a chosen parameter; fixture recovery measured 2026-09-30, `pytest packages/bkt/analyze/tests/test_marketing.py -k season`] |
| Anomalies | median-MAD z on daily totals: abs(x - median) / (1.4826 x MAD) > 3.5 | [empirical: cutoff from Iglewicz and Hoaglin 1993, a chosen parameter; spike recall and flat-series silence measured 2026-09-30, `pytest packages/bkt/analyze/tests/test_marketing.py -k anomaly`] |

No causal claims. Attribution is labelled a heuristic. `bm.py check` certifies the Rat definitions and theorems only. The Python float code is tied to them by a differential test that recomputes every ratio metric on every fixture with `fractions.Fraction` and asserts agreement within 1e-9 relative, and asserts null exactly where the Lean `ratio` returns none.

## Storage and privacy

- Upload reuses the existing import storage path and page code: browser hashes, uploads to private bucket `research-os-imports` under `<owner>/<sha256>`, `POST /api/research-os/import` verifies bytes and records `graph.import_files`. The quota trigger caps 500 objects and 2 GiB per owner. Privacy per user: the marketing route creates its imports itself with `node_id` null (kind `dataset`, `source.marketing = true`), so `graph.can_read_import_object`, which joins through `graph.nodes`, admits no grantee and no public reader. The storage key is `<owner>/<sha256>`, shared by any import of the same bytes; if that path is also recorded under an import whose node is public or granted, the route refuses with 409 `object_shared` and names the other import. SQL test: a grantee of an unrelated node cannot read a marketing object, and anon cannot.
- Size: the bucket takes 50 MB; marketing analysis caps each file at 16 MB (the desktop jobs cap) and 64 MB per analysis, checked from the recorded bytes before download, and 1,000,000 rows, enforced inside the readers.
- Upload checks, client and server: extension allowlist (csv, tsv, xlsx, json, jsonl, parquet, pdf), declared MIME normalized, and server-side magic bytes on the stored object (`PK\x03\x04` for xlsx, `%PDF-` for pdf, `PAR1` for parquet, UTF-8 decodable and no NUL in the first 64 KB for text). Mismatch returns 415 and nothing runs.
- Encryption at rest: the raw object relies on storage-layer encryption (hosted Supabase encrypts storage at rest; the local stack relies on an encrypted host disk, stated in docs/AUTH.md and unverified by code). Derived output is sealed in the app layer. DDL:

```
graph.marketing_reports (
  id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(),
  import_id uuid not null references graph.imports(id) on delete cascade,
  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,
  input_digest text not null,        -- sha256 over the sorted file sha256 list
  analyzer_version text not null,    -- pysrc version hash
  key_id text not null,
  iv bytea not null, ciphertext bytea not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (import_id, input_digest, analyzer_version)
)
```

RLS on, no policy, service role only, revoked from anon and authenticated. AES-256-GCM, key from HKDF-SHA256 over the key named by `key_id` with the owner id as info, random 96-bit IV, AAD = owner id, import id, input digest. Keys come from `MARKETING_SEAL_KEYS` (`id:base64,...`, first is current); rotation adds a key at the front and old rows keep decrypting. Insert uses `on conflict do nothing` then reads the row, so a double click or retry returns the same report. `GET /api/research-os/marketing?import=<id>` decrypts and returns the saved report. Missing or malformed key config: POST and GET fail closed with 503 `seal_key_missing` before any analysis runs.
- Delete on request: `DELETE /api/research-os/marketing?import=<id>` removes each storage object of that import that no other `graph.import_files` row names, the `graph.imports` row (cascading `import_files` and `marketing_reports`), and returns counts. Storage removal failure returns 502 and leaves rows so a retry can finish. Account deletion cascades through `auth.users`.
- No third parties: the route spawns local Python only; no fetch to any host. A test asserts the route module imports no HTTP client and the Python package imports no network module.
- No logging of uploads: route errors log the error code only, never file names, cell values or report content; the route never forwards Python stderr. In marketing mode the Python side catches every exception at the top and prints one error code; temp dirs are 0700 and removed in `finally`. Test: a failing parse of a file holding a marker string leaves the marker out of captured console output and stderr.
- Output escaping: the web report renders through React text nodes only, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; the Markdown report escapes `|`, backticks, `<`, `>` and `[` in user values. Test: a campaign named `<script>alert(1)</script>` and a cell `=HYPERLINK("x")` come out inert in both.
- Retention: storage deletion is immediate. Hosted Supabase backups keep deleted rows and objects until the backup window expires (the plan's tier sets it); the local stack keeps no backups. The page states both.
- Desktop: `bkt analyze` keeps writing to the 0700 analyses directory. Desktop at-rest encryption of saved reports is out of scope (packages/bkt/src is owned by another agent) and filed as a bead.

## Surfaces

- Web: `src/app/research-os/(app)/import/marketing/page.tsx` (staff-only at launch) reuses the import page's hashing, upload and attach helpers (extracted to `src/lib/research-os/import-client.ts`, the import page switches to it with no behavior change), then calls the marketing route and renders the report with a delete button. Behind `staffOnlyAtLaunch` like the import route.
- Desktop: `bkt analyze file.xlsx` works through the Python core with no TS change. The desktop jobs input allowlist (`job-specs.ts`, owned by PR #429) needs `.xlsx`, `.parquet`, `.pdf` added; filed as a bead for after #429 merges.
- bkt-ui Import view: unchanged in this PR; a bead covers linking it to the analyze job once the allowlist lands.

## Tests

- Python `tests/test_marketing.py`: locale numbers, UTF-16 BOM, offset timestamps, lying zip headers caught by the counting stream, row cap truncation, Fraction differential, escaping, the Meta plus Shopify join; each adapter fixture detects the right platform and matches expected metrics; XLSX formula cell yields cached value and never evaluates; zip bomb, macro workbook, DOCTYPE part, and wrong magic are rejected; PDF fixture parses to the expected table; zero-denominator metrics return null; cohort retention in [0, 1]; mix sums to 1 within 1e-9; attribution totals equal conversion totals; anomaly detector flags an injected spike and nothing on a flat series.
- TS vitest: magic-byte check, size caps, 429 and 503 under the limiter, timeout kill, 409 `object_shared`, shared-object survival on delete, idempotent re-POST, 503 `seal_key_missing`, key rotation decrypt, route auth (401 unauthenticated, 404 on another owner's import), 503 when `BKT_ANALYZE_PYTHON` unset, seal round trip and AAD mismatch failure, delete path including storage failure, no-network import assertion, parity with the CLI output.
- SQL test `supabase/tests/research_os_marketing_reports.sql`: RLS denies another owner, cascade on import delete.
- Lean: `bm.py check` passes with the new module.
- Existing suites: `packages/bkt/analyze/tests`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `tsc`.

## Rollout

Additive: one migration (`graph.marketing_reports`, service-role only, cascade), new route, new page, new Python modules. Staff-only at launch through the existing gate. Rollback: revert the PR and drop the table; no existing table changes.

{"design":"Restart spec, founder 2026-09-30. It replaces design v1, which is kept in the bead history.

Shell. /explore uses the canon search shell unchanged: search, filters and sorts on the left or top center, and the right nav with full information and links. /canon/search itself does not change. The only new part is the center component: a full-page component centred in the available space.

Center component. One rendering framework for every data set: canon excerpts, advisors and every downloaded corpus.
1 Circle chart. A data set's fields map to the PCA or SVD circle chart of the prime-directions and advisor tools: spokes are components, and each observation is a polygon of its standardized scores. Sparse or non-numeric data, such as tokens, is integrated to fill the full distribution, so the circle can be smooth numerically. Averages across the data set's observations are drawn on the same chart.
2 Slices. The circle charts stack as slices in a locked higher view, left to right and back to front. Scrolling steps through them like a file system, and selecting one goes straight to its circle chart. A transparent cylinder encloses the stack.
3 Cylinder. The full cylinder is the slices joined into one smooth surface.
4 Sphere, and sphere through time: these already exist in the solvability atlas.
5 Helix. It shows events through time, or any circle chart swept along one variable such as time. Sequences show as a helix or as slices. The helicoid is for DNA.
6 3D polar plots, using radius, polar distance and charge, and experiments running through time.
Interaction: click to select. On a single circle chart, scrolling steps through its variable, such as advisor or time.

Basis: the canon search components plus both advisor tools (the prime-directions advisor page and the bkt desktop Advisors view), through one adapter. The existing renders to reuse: the prime-directions radar, and the solvability atlas SliceCircle, SolvabilitySpace, cylinder, sphere and helix (#442)."}

{"design":"Restart spec, founder 2026-09-30. It replaces design v1, which is kept in the bead history.

Shell. /explore uses the canon search shell unchanged: search, filters and sorts on the left or top center, and the right nav with full information and links. /canon/search itself does not change. The only new part is the center component: a full-page component centred in the available space.

Center component. One rendering framework for every data set: canon excerpts, advisors and every downloaded corpus.
1 Circle chart. A data set's fields map to the PCA or SVD circle chart of the prime-directions and advisor tools: spokes are components, and each observation is a polygon of its standardized scores. Sparse or non-numeric data, such as tokens, is integrated to fill the full distribution, so the circle can be smooth numerically. Averages across the data set's observations are drawn on the same chart.
2 Slices. The circle charts stack as slices in a locked higher view, left to right and back to front. Scrolling steps through them like a file system, and selecting one goes straight to its circle chart. A transparent cylinder encloses the stack.
3 Cylinder. The full cylinder is the slices joined into one smooth surface.
4 Sphere, and sphere through time: these already exist in the solvability atlas.
5 Helix. It shows events through time, or any circle chart swept along one variable such as time. Sequences show as a helix or as slices. The helicoid is for DNA.
6 3D polar plots, using radius, polar distance and charge, and experiments running through time.
Interaction: click to select. On a single circle chart, scrolling steps through its variable, such as advisor or time.

Basis: the canon search components plus both advisor tools (the prime-directions advisor page and the bkt desktop Advisors view), through one adapter. The existing renders to reuse: the prime-directions radar, and the solvability atlas SliceCircle, SolvabilitySpace, cylinder, sphere and helix (#442).
7 Stepper. Replace every list of item buttons (advisor names, event names, slice labels) with one drag scrubber: a thin track with a handle, plus the current item's label and index (for example "Lascaux cave paintings 1 / 260"). Dragging the handle and scrolling both move it. In every view, including the globe and sphere views, when there is a variable to step such as time, scroll steps it. Scroll never changes the size, zoom or orientation of the globe.
8 Home globe. Everything the home page globe at / does is folded into /explore: its scrubber, events, markers and interactions."}

Sparse or non-numeric data, such as tokens, is integrated to fill the full distribution, so the circle can be smooth numerically. Averages across the data set's observations are drawn on the same chart.
2 Slices. The circle charts stack as slices in a locked higher view, left to right and back to front. Scrolling steps through them like a file system, and selecting one goes straight to its circle chart. A transparent cylinder encloses the stack.
3 Cylinder. The full cylinder is the slices joined into one smooth surface.
4 Sphere, and sphere through time: these already exist in the solvability atlas.
5 Helix. It shows events through time, or any circle chart swept along one variable such as time. Sequences show as a helix or as slices. The helicoid is for DNA.
6 3D polar plots, using radius, polar distance and charge, and experiments running through time.
Interaction: click to select. On a single circle chart, scrolling steps through its variable, such as advisor or time.

Basis: the canon search components plus both advisor tools (the prime-directions advisor page and the bkt desktop Advisors view), through one adapter. The existing renders to reuse: the prime-directions radar, and the solvability atlas SliceCircle, SolvabilitySpace, cylinder, sphere and helix (#442).
7 Stepper. Replace every list of item buttons (advisor names, event names, slice labels) with one drag scrubber: a thin track with a handle, plus the current item's label and index (for example "Lascaux cave paintings 1 / 260"). Dragging the handle and scrolling both move it. In every view, including the globe and sphere views, when there is a variable to step such as time, scroll steps it. Scroll never changes the size, zoom or orientation of the globe.
8 Home globe. Everything the home page globe at / does is folded into /explore: its scrubber, events, markers and interactions.
9 Full screen. As on the home page, the main component expands to full screen. It sits underneath the nav bars and the other components, and in full screen the search, filters, scrubber and right nav float on top of it or inside it as rounded-corner widgets. An exit control, plus Esc, returns to the normal layout. One Next.js route, /explore, that runs canon search (src/app/api/canon/search, CanonGlobeMount) and advisor search (advisor-review.ts, prime-directions people file) through one query box and one shared scene.
